role.altitude: The cytogenetic technologist keeps counting, identifying abnormalities, choosing cultures and checking meaning; searching slides, sorting karyograms, writing notation and typing details shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A technologist who spends the day at the microscope on hard cases.

tasks.short: Scan slides for good metaphases, count numbers of chromosomes, capture images and arrange the karyogram, identify the structural abnormalities from banding patterns through microscopes, record counts and findings and discuss unclear findings with the cytogeneticist.

steps.what: Technologist scans culture slides under the microscope for good metaphases
Technologist counts numbers of chromosomes in each metaphase
Technologist captures images and arranges the karyogram by cutting and sorting chromosomes on screen

loop.output: A proposed karyogram with each chromosome placed in its pair.
loop.check: The technologist checks every placement and moves wrong ones.
loop.stop: Poor-quality metaphases are arranged by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Chromosome shapes and bands vary per cell.

steps.what: Technologist identifies the structural abnormalities by comparing banding patterns
Technologist records counts and findings on the worksheet
Technologist discusses unclear findings with the cytogeneticist

tasks.design: An automated slide scanner finds candidate metaphases for the technologist to choose, and karyotyping software proposes the karyogram, which the technologist checks chromosome by chromosome. Counting, finding abnormalities, recording and the cytogeneticist talk stay with the technologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Metaphases were found by eye and karyograms arranged by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Metaphase finders and chromosome classification software.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a small translocation others miss.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and sorting; diagnosis judgement stays.

evidence.claim: ASI HiBand classifies chromosomes for karyograms.
At the AON lab in the US, HiBand cut karyogram analysis time by 35 to 40%.
Software with a medical purpose is a medical device under the MDR.
AI in MDR and IVDR devices is high-risk under the AI Act if a notified body must assess it.
Automated slide scanners locate metaphases for review.

assumptions: Boundary: counting and identifying; examining chromosomes to detect abnormalities in general (task 17385) is a sibling task.
s3 keeps 62, from the 35-40% analysis saving at AON. s1 keeps 60 because the technologist still reviews and chooses metaphases. Counting and identifying keep their full time.
The means prior puts 80% in person; the steps show 70%, because karyogram work is on screen (25%).
research_questions: Does the lab already use a metaphase finder?

incremental.description: Technologist loads slide trays into the scanner and handles scan errors.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the lab already uses a metaphase finder (s1 keeps 90) and many proposed karyograms need rearranging (s3 keeps 85) (5.2); high: manual search and arrangement today (17.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review karyogram, FISH and aCGH data, write the ISCN string by hand, check its syntax against the ISCN manual, describe results in plain words, have a second technologist check the ISCN against what was seen and discuss with the cytogeneticist to describe results in International System of Cytogenetic Nomenclature language.

steps.what: Technologist reviews the karyogram, FISH and aCGH data
Technologist writes the International System of Cytogenetic Nomenclature string for each result by hand
Technologist checks the string's syntax against the ISCN manual
Technologist describes the result in plain words
Second technologist checks that the ISCN string and description match what was seen, not only the syntax
Technologist discusses the result with the cytogeneticist

tasks.design: The technologist records the karyotype as structured entries (chromosome, band, type of change), and the system builds the ISCN string from them and checks its syntax by rule, instead of the technologist writing and checking it by hand. Reviewing data, the plain-word description, the second technologist's check of meaning and the cytogeneticist talk stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: ISCN strings were written and syntax-checked by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: ISCN strings generated from structured karyotype entries, with syntax rules.
tasks.still_hard: Complex rearrangements with no simple notation.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the string says what the cell shows.
tasks.altitude: Less notation work; meaning stays with people.

evidence.claim: ISCN strings can be generated from structured karyotype data.
Software with a medical purpose is a medical device under the MDR.

assumptions: Boundary: ISCN description. Summarizing and reporting results (task 17376) is a sibling task, and the release of the report belongs there.
s2 keeps 30 for entering the structured karyotype and complex cases; s3 keeps 30. The second check covers meaning and keeps its full time.
The means prior puts 43% on documents; the steps show 55%, because notation and description are written work.
research_questions: What share of karyotypes fit structured entry?

incremental.description: Technologist keeps the notation rules current with ISCN editions.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many complex cases do not fit the structured entries, so strings are still written and checked by hand (s2 and s3 keep 60) (14.5); high: mostly standard karyotypes (25.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the referral form, type patient and referral details into the laboratory system, write specimen receipt details in the paper log, type the log into the system, hand-label culture flasks and slides, check entries and phone senders about missing details to input details of specimens into logs or computer systems.

steps.what: Technologist reads the referral form for patient, specimen type and reason
Technologist types patient and referral details from the paper form into the laboratory system
Technologist writes specimen receipt time, volume and condition in the paper specimen log
Technologist types the specimen log into the laboratory system
Technologist writes labels for culture flasks and slides by hand
Technologist checks entered details against the referral
Technologist phones the sender about missing details

tasks.design: Requesting hospitals send electronic orders with patient and referral details. Receipt details are entered at the receiving bench straight into the laboratory system instead of a paper log, and the system prints barcode labels for flasks and slides. With less typing there is less to check. Reading referrals, the receipt record and calls to senders stay with the technologist; saving entries is an ordinary save and needs no approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Details were typed from paper forms and logs, and labels handwritten.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic orders, bench entry and barcode label printing.
tasks.still_hard: Senders who still use paper forms.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a referral that does not fit the specimen.

evidence.claim: Laboratory systems accept electronic orders and print barcode labels.
Fax may not be used to share medical data.

assumptions: Boundary: specimen details at receipt. Logging processing, analysis and technical issues (task 20568) is a sibling task.
Coverage: s2 keeps 25 for senders on paper; s4 keeps 10; s5 keeps 30 for special vessels; s6 keeps 50. The receipt record in s3 is the first record and keeps its full time.
The means prior puts 41% in person; the steps show 12%, because data entry is screen and paper work.
research_questions: What share of senders can send electronic orders?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many senders keep paper referrals (s2 keeps 60), bench entry is used for half of receipts (s4 keeps 50) and more entries need checking (s6 keeps 75) (26.9); high: mostly electronic orders (43.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read specimen type and reason for referral, look up the protocol in the procedure binder, select the appropriate culturing system or procedure, discuss unusual referrals with the cytogeneticist, set up cultures and note the chosen procedure.

steps.what: Technologist reads the specimen type and reason for referral
Technologist looks up the protocol for the indication in the procedure binder
Technologist selects the appropriate culturing system or procedure
Technologist discusses unusual referrals with the cytogeneticist
Technologist sets up cultures
Technologist notes the chosen procedure in the laboratory system

tasks.design: The laboratory system proposes the protocol from the specimen type and indication code using the lab's own rule table, instead of a binder lookup; the technologist confirms or changes it. Reading the referral, choosing, the cytogeneticist talk, setting up cultures and the note stay with the technologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Protocols were looked up in a binder.
tasks.enabler_now: Rule tables from specimen type and indication to protocol.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a sample needs a non-standard culture.

evidence.claim: A rule table can map specimen type and indication to a lab protocol.

assumptions: Boundary: selecting the culture procedure; choosing banding methods (task 17378) is a sibling task.
s2 keeps 40 for referrals outside the table.
The means prior puts 70% in person; the steps show 60%, because reading referrals and lookups take 35%.

incremental.description: Technologist keeps the rule table current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many unusual referrals fall outside the rule table (s2 keeps 75) (3.5); high: mostly standard indications (8.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
